citations.claim: energy at first violating step exceeds allowed 4089 J, 6x increase with no controller work
body 1 speed more than tripled after collision, showing energy injection
body 0 retains high speed instead of losing energy in inelastic collision

counterfactual.change: Flipped bodies[0].vx from +42.03 to -42.03 (one field) so bodies move apart and do not collide in the single step; energy then conserved at ~3712 J and no violation occurs, proving the violation requires the high-speed collision.

explanation: Shrunk scenario has two circles on near-head-on trajectory with relative speed ~58 m/s and gap 0.058. In one dt (0.00357s, 6 substeps) they collide and energy jumps from 3712 J to 23651 J (6.3x) despite restitution <1 and no controller work. Post-collision speeds increase: body 1 from 16.3 to 51.8 m/s and body 0 remains ~38 m/s, indicating impulse added energy instead of removing it. Flipping body 0 vx to -42 to make bodies separate removes collision and energy stays conserved, confirming collision response is cause. Likely sign or restitution term error in impulse magnitude / velocity update that injects energy when normal relative velocity is large.
vision_note: Tile 0 shows two blue circular bodies positioned very close together near the bottom-right with only a tiny gap between them. Tile 1 shows them still essentially in contact with slightly increased overlap, consistent with a collision occurring between the two successive steps and no walls or waypoints present.
